questions.stem: After how many years is the Census of India conducted?
questions.explanation: The Census of India is a decennial exercise, meaning it counts the whole population once every ten years. Between two Censuses the figures are only estimates, so the ten-year interval is the basis for measuring decadal growth.

optionRationale.2: A five-year gap is used by some surveys and plans, not by the Census.
optionRationale.3: Seven years is not a cycle used for the Census.
optionRationale.4: Fifteen years is longer than the actual Census interval.

questions.stem: Among the Indian states, which one has the highest density of population as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Bihar has the highest density among the states, because it has a very large population living in a relatively small, fertile part of the Ganga plain. Uttar Pradesh is far larger in area, and Kerala and Haryana have lower densities.

optionRationale.1: Uttar Pradesh has the largest population among states but a larger area, so its density is lower.
optionRationale.3: Kerala is densely settled but its density is below Bihar's.
optionRationale.4: Haryana's density is much lower than Bihar's.

questions.stem: Which language, among those listed in the Eighth Schedule, is spoken as mother tongue by the largest number of people in India?
questions.explanation: Hindi has the largest number of speakers among the scheduled languages, mostly in the northern and central states. Bengali, Telugu and Marathi each have many speakers but fewer than Hindi. Hence the correct answer is: Hindi.

optionRationale.1: Bengali has many speakers but fewer than Hindi.
optionRationale.2: Telugu is spoken mainly in two states and has fewer speakers than Hindi.
optionRationale.4: Marathi is largely confined to Maharashtra and has fewer speakers than Hindi.

questions.objective: Recall the linguistic composition of India

questions.stem: The sex ratio of a population is defined as the number of
questions.explanation: In India the sex ratio is expressed as the number of females per 1000 males. A value above 1000 means females outnumber males, and a value below 1000 means males are more numerous.

optionRationale.1: That is the reverse of the Indian convention used in the Census.
optionRationale.2: The Indian convention uses 1000 males, not 100.
optionRationale.3: That describes density, not sex ratio.

questions.stem: Fishing, mining and forestry are classified in which sector of the economy?
questions.explanation: Primary activities take resources directly from nature. Agriculture, fishing, forestry and mining all belong here. Secondary activities process raw material, while tertiary and quaternary activities provide services and knowledge-based work. Hence the correct answer is: Primary sector.

optionRationale.2: Secondary activities manufacture or process goods.
optionRationale.3: Tertiary activities are services such as trade and transport.
optionRationale.4: Quaternary activities are knowledge-based work such as research.

questions.stem: A high dependency ratio in a region generally means
options: more working persons than dependants in the region, so a lighter burden on workers
a heavier economic burden on the working-age population
a lower share of children and old persons in the total population of the region
a higher literacy rate among all the age groups
questions.explanation: The dependency ratio compares dependants (children and elderly) with the working-age group. When it is high, each worker has to support more dependants, which strains household income and public services. Hence the correct answer is: a heavier economic burden on the working-age population.

optionRationale.1: More workers than dependents would give a low ratio.
optionRationale.3: A low share of dependants gives a low ratio.
optionRationale.4: The ratio is about age groups, not about literacy.

questions.stem: For the calculation of literacy rate in the Census, a person is treated as literate if he or she is aged
options: 5 years or above and can sign his or her name only
15 years or above and has passed primary school
7 years or above and can read and write with understanding
3 years or above and attends a school regularly
questions.explanation: In the Census a person aged seven or above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is literate. Children below seven are not counted in the literacy rate calculation, and a mere signature is not enough.

optionRationale.1: Signing the name only is not literacy, and the age limit is seven.
optionRationale.2: Passing a school grade is not required and the age is not fifteen.
optionRationale.4: Literacy needs the ability to read and write, not just attendance.

questions.objective: Recall the Census definition of literacy

questions.stem: As per Census 2011, the share of rural population in the total population of India is
options: about one-half of the total population
less than one-third of the total population
nearly nine-tenths of the total population
questions.explanation: India is still predominantly rural, with a little under seven-tenths of its people living in villages as per Census 2011. The urban share has been increasing slowly from one Census to the next, but the majority is rural.

optionRationale.1: The rural share is clearly higher than half.
optionRationale.2: The urban share is under one-third, so the rural share is not that low.
optionRationale.3: Nine-tenths is far above the Census figure.

questions.stem: A person who has worked for less than 183 days (about six months) in the year is classified in the Census as a
options: main worker, one employed for more than half the year
non-worker, a person with no work at all
cultivator, one who tills his own or leased land
questions.explanation: The Census divides workers into main workers, who worked for most of the year (183 days or more), and marginal workers, who worked for less than that period. Persons who did no work are non-workers.

optionRationale.2: A main worker works for at least 183 days.
optionRationale.3: A non-worker did no work at all.
optionRationale.4: A cultivator is an occupational category, not defined by days worked.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the religious composition of India as per Census 2011.
A. Hindus form the majority of the population.
B. Muslims form the largest religious minority.
C. Christians are the second largest religious minority.
D. Sikhs are more numerous than Christians.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Hindus form the majority, Muslims are the largest minority and Christians come next. Sikhs form a smaller share than Christians, so statement D is wrong. Hence A, B and C are correct.

optionRationale.1: Option 1 leaves out C, which is correct.
optionRationale.3: Option 3 includes D, which is wrong, and leaves out A.
optionRationale.4: Option 4 includes D, which is wrong.

questions.stem: A district has an area of 400 square kilometres and a density of 750 persons per square kilometre. What is its population?
questions.explanation: Density equals population divided by area, so population equals density times area. That is 750 persons per square kilometre multiplied by 400 square kilometres, which gives 3,00,000 persons in the district. Hence the correct answer is: 3,00,000.

optionRationale.2: 2,50,000 results from dividing instead of multiplying correctly.
optionRationale.4: 1,50,000 is half of the correct figure.

questions.objective: Use the density formula in reverse

questions.stem: In a district the sex ratio is 950 females per 1000 males and there are 1,20,000 males. How many females are there?
questions.explanation: A sex ratio of 950 means 950 females for every 1000 males. So the number of females is 1,20,000 multiplied by 950 and divided by 1000, which equals 1,14,000. Hence the correct answer is: 1,14,000.

optionRationale.1: 1,26,316 results from dividing by 0.95 instead of multiplying.
optionRationale.2: 1,20,000 would need a sex ratio of 1000.
optionRationale.3: 1,08,000 comes from using a ratio of 900.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The work participation rate of women in India is lower than that of men.
Reason (R): Many household and unpaid domestic activities done by women are not recorded as economic work in the Census.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The work participation rate counts workers as a share of population. A good part of women's work is domestic or unpaid, and it is not counted as work in the economic sense, which lowers the recorded rate. So R explains A.

optionRationale.2: R is a direct explanation of A, so option 2 is wrong.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so option 3 is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so option 4 is wrong.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The population of India is evenly spread over all its states and regions.
Reason (R): The Himalayan and Thar desert regions have very low density while the Ganga plain has very high density.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Population in India is highly uneven. The plains with fertile soil and water support dense settlement, while mountains and deserts have sparse population. So the assertion is false, but the reason is a true statement.

optionRationale.1: Option 1 is wrong because A is false, so R cannot explain it.
optionRationale.2: Option 2 is wrong because A is false.
optionRationale.3: Option 3 is wrong because R is true.

questions.objective: Recognise the uneven distribution of population

right: III. Workers as a percentage of the total population

questions.explanation: Sex ratio is females per 1000 males (I), density is persons per unit area (II), work participation rate is workers as a percentage of the population (III) and the dependency ratio is dependants per 100 working-age persons (IV).

optionRationale.1: It swaps sex ratio and density.
optionRationale.2: It swaps work participation rate and dependency ratio.

questions.explanation: Fishing takes a resource from nature (primary, II). Textile manufacturing processes raw material (secondary, IV). Banking is a service (tertiary, I) and scientific research is a knowledge-based activity (quaternary, III).

optionRationale.2: It swaps the sectors of textile manufacturing and banking.
optionRationale.3: It makes textile manufacturing tertiary and banking secondary.
optionRationale.4: It makes fishing tertiary, which is wrong.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about age composition in India.
A. Persons aged 0 to 14 years are counted as young dependants.
B. Persons aged 15 to 59 years form the working-age group.
C. Persons aged 60 years and above are counted as aged dependants.
D. The dependency ratio rises when the share of the working-age group rises.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The three age groups used in the Census are 0 to 14 (young), 15 to 59 (working) and 60 and above (aged). The dependency ratio falls, not rises, when the working-age share rises, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Option 1 leaves out C, which is correct.
optionRationale.2: Option 2 includes D, which is wrong, and leaves out A and C.
optionRationale.4: Option 4 includes D, which is wrong.

questions.stem: The population of a district was 40 lakh and it grew by 20 per cent in a decade. In the next decade the district added the same number of persons as in the first decade. What was the growth rate in the second decade (nearest figure)?
questions.explanation: The first decade added 8 lakh, bringing the population to 48 lakh. Adding another 8 lakh gives a growth of 8 divided by 48, about 16.7 per cent. So the percentage falls even though the absolute gain is unchanged.

optionRationale.1: 20 per cent wrongly uses the original base.
optionRationale.3: 25 per cent divides by a wrong base.
optionRationale.4: 14.3 per cent divides 8 by 56, using the final population.

questions.objective: Compare growth rate and absolute increase

questions.stem: Which of the following is a main reason for the rise in the share of urban population in India?
options: A fall in the death rate of urban areas alone
A steady decline in the number of towns and cities
A shrinking of the service sector in all the cities
Rural-to-urban migration and the reclassification of villages as towns
questions.explanation: The urban share rises when people move from villages to cities for work and services, and when large villages meet census criteria and are reclassified as towns. Both lift the proportion of the total population that is urban.

optionRationale.1: Falling death rates alone do not raise the urban share relative to rural areas.
optionRationale.2: The number of towns has increased, not declined.
optionRationale.3: The service sector has been growing and draws people to towns.
